explanation: C = Kε₀A/d = K times capacitance without dielectric (C₀ = ε₀A/d).

subject: physics

explanation: Angle of dip (inclination) is 90° at magnetic poles where field lines are vertical.

subject: physics

question: The unit of magnetic dipole moment is:
explanation: Magnetic dipole moment m = IA has units Ampere-meter² (Am²).

subject: physics

description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The electric potential due to a point charge q at distance r is:
explanation: V = q/4πε₀r (scalar quantity).

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The resistance of a conductor depends on:
explanation: Resistance R = ρL/A, where ρ is resistivity (depends on material), L is length, and A is cross-sectional area. Therefore, resistance depends on all three factors.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance C charged to potential difference V is:
explanation: Energy stored U = ½QV = ½(CV)V = ½CV², where Q = CV is the charge on the capacitor.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is:
explanation: Inside a long solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform, parallel to the axis of the solenoid, and has magnitude B = μ₀nI, where n is number of turns per unit length and I is current.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: According to Ohm's law, current through a conductor is:
explanation: Ohm's law states that for a conductor at constant temperature, current (I) is directly proportional to potential difference (V): V ∝ I or V = IR.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The electric field intensity at a point due to a point charge Q is proportional to:
explanation: Electric field E = kQ/r², so E ∝ Q (for fixed distance r).

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The electric potential at a point due to a point charge Q is proportional to:
explanation: Electric potential V = kQ/r, so V ∝ Q and V ∝ 1/r.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The power dissipated in a resistor of resistance R carrying current I is:
explanation: Power P = VI = (IR)I = I²R (using Ohm's law V = IR).

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor increases when:
explanation: Capacitance C = ε₀KA/d, where K is dielectric constant. Inserting a dielectric (K > 1) increases capacitance. Decreasing area or increasing separation decreases capacitance.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The equivalent capacitance of two 6 μF capacitors connected in series is:
explanation: For series combination: 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ = 1/6 + 1/6 = 2/6 = 1/3. Therefore, C = 3 μF.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The magnetic susceptibility of a diamagnetic substance is:
explanation: Diamagnetic substances have small negative susceptibility (χ ≈ -10⁻⁵), independent of temperature. They are weakly repelled by magnetic fields.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The electric field inside a charged conducting sphere is:
explanation: In electrostatic conditions, electric field inside a conductor is zero. All excess charge resides on the outer surface.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The power factor in an AC circuit containing resistance and inductance is:
explanation: Power factor = cosφ = R/Z, where R is resistance and Z is impedance. For RL circuit, 0 < cosφ < 1 (lagging).

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The electric flux through a closed surface enclosing a charge Q is:
explanation: Gauss's law: Φ = Q/ε₀, where Q is net charge enclosed by the Gaussian surface.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The magnetic moment of a current loop of area A carrying current I is:
explanation: Magnetic moment μ = IA, with direction given by right-hand rule (perpendicular to plane of loop).

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The electric field due to an infinite plane sheet of charge is:
explanation: For infinite sheet with uniform surface charge density σ: E = σ/2ε₀, constant at all distances from the sheet.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The electric dipole moment of two charges +q and -q separated by distance d is:
explanation: Electric dipole moment p = qd, direction from negative to positive charge.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The energy stored in a capacitor is in the form of:
explanation: Energy in capacitor is stored in the electric field between the plates: U = ½ε₀E² × volume.

question: The number of electrons in 1 coulomb of charge is approximately:
explanation: Charge of electron e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Number of electrons n = Q/e = 1/(1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 6.25 × 10¹⁸.

subject: physics

explanation: Diamagnetic materials have small negative susceptibility (χ < 0, typically ~ -10^-5). Paramagnetic: small positive; ferromagnetic: large positive.

explanation: Time constant τ = RC for charging/discharging of capacitor through resistor. After τ, capacitor charges to ~63% of max voltage.

explanation: Balance condition: P/Q = R/S (ratio of resistances in opposite arms equal). No current flows through galvanometer at balance.

explanation: Angle of dip (inclination) is 90° at magnetic poles where field lines are vertical; 0° at magnetic equator where field lines are horizontal.

subject: physics

question: The antiparticle of electron is:
explanation: Positron (e⁺) has same mass as electron but positive charge. Discovered by Anderson in cosmic rays (1932).

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The ionizing power is maximum for:
explanation: Ionizing power: α > β > γ. Alpha has large mass and charge, creates dense ionization along short path.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The reactance of pure inductor in AC circuit is:
explanation: Inductive reactance X_L = ωL = 2πfL. Current lags voltage by 90°.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The reactance of pure capacitor in AC circuit is:
explanation: Capacitive reactance X_C = 1/ωC = 1/(2πfC). Current leads voltage by 90°.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The average power in AC circuit is given by:
explanation: Average power P_avg = V_rms I_rms cosφ, where φ = phase angle between voltage and current. cosφ = power factor.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The rms value of AC voltage V = V₀ sinωt is:
explanation: V_rms = V₀/√2 for sinusoidal AC. Similarly I_rms = I₀/√2.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The principle of transformer is based on:
explanation: Transformer works on mutual induction between primary and secondary coils linked by changing magnetic flux.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: For step-up transformer:
explanation: Step-up transformer increases voltage: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p > 1, so N_s > N_p. Current decreases proportionally (ignoring losses).

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The efficiency of practical transformer is typically:
explanation: Large power transformers have efficiency 95-99% due to low losses (copper, iron, hysteresis, eddy current).

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The energy stored in magnetic field per unit volume is:
explanation: Energy density u_B = B²/2μ₀ in vacuum (analogous to u_E = ½ε₀E² for electric field).

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The displacement current was introduced by Maxwell to:
explanation: Displacement current I_d = ε₀(dΦ_E/dt) completes circuit during capacitor charging and modifies Ampere's law to Ampere-Maxwell law.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following rays are deflected by an electric field?
explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons, which are negatively charged particles. Therefore, they are deflected by both electric and magnetic fields. X-rays, gamma rays, and neutrons are uncharged and are not deflected.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If the charge on a capacitor is doubled, its capacitance:
explanation: Capacitance (C) is a geometric property of the capacitor (C = ε₀A/d). It depends on the area of plates and the distance between them, not on the charge (Q) or voltage (V). C = Q/V, but if Q is doubled, V also doubles, keeping C constant.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The electric field lines point:
option1: From lower potential to higher potential
option2: From higher potential to lower potential
explanation: By convention, electric field lines start at positive charges (high potential) and end at negative charges (low potential). They point in the direction of decreasing electric potential.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Three capacitors of equal capacitance C are connected in parallel. The equivalent capacitance is:
explanation: When capacitors are connected in parallel, the equivalent capacitance is the sum of individual capacitances. For three capacitors each of value C, C_eq = C + C + C = 3C.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: According to Ohm's law, the current through a conductor is directly proportional to:
explanation: Ohm's law states that at constant temperature, the current (I) flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (V) applied across its ends. V ∝ I, or V = IR.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: An ammeter is always connected in:
explanation: An ammeter measures current. To measure the current flowing through a branch, the ammeter must be connected in series so that the entire current of that branch passes through it. It has very low resistance.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The heating effect of current is given by:
explanation: All three formulas are equivalent and can be derived from Joule's law of heating (H = I²Rt) by using Ohm's law V = IR. H = I²Rt = (V/R)² R t = V²t/R = VIt.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The mutual inductance between two coils depends on:
explanation: Mutual inductance (M) is a measure of the ability of one coil to induce an EMF in another. It depends on the geometry (size, shape, number of turns) of the coils, their relative positions, and the magnetic properties of the core material.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The peak value of an AC voltage is 311 V. Its RMS value is approximately:
explanation: The RMS value of a sinusoidal AC is related to the peak value by V_rms = V_peak / √2. √2 ≈ 1.414. So, V_rms = 311 / 1.414 ≈ 220 V.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In a transformer, if the number of turns in the primary is less than in the secondary, it is a:
explanation: A transformer works on the principle of mutual induction. The voltage ratio is equal to the turns ratio: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p. If N_s > N_p, then V_s > V_p, so it is a step-up transformer.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The impedance of an AC circuit containing only a pure capacitor is:
explanation: Impedance (Z) is the total opposition to current in an AC circuit. For a pure capacitor, the opposition is called capacitive reactance, given by Xc = 1/(ωC) = 1/(2πfC).

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The internal resistance of an ideal voltmeter is:
explanation: An ideal voltmeter should not draw any current from the circuit it is measuring. To achieve this, it must have infinite resistance so that it acts as an open circuit and measures the true potential difference.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Two parallel plate capacitors of capacitance C and 2C are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance is:
explanation: For capacitors in series, 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂. So, 1/C_eq = 1/C + 1/(2C) = (2+1)/(2C) = 3/(2C). Therefore, C_eq = 2C/3.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A 10 Ω resistor carries a current of 2 A. The power dissipated in it is:
explanation: Power dissipated in a resistor can be calculated using P = I²R. Here, I = 2 A and R = 10 Ω. So, P = (2)² × 10 = 4 × 10 = 40 W.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The time constant of an RC circuit is given by:
explanation: The time constant (τ) of an RC circuit is the time required to charge the capacitor to approximately 63.2% of its final value (or discharge to 36.8%). It is given by the product of resistance and capacitance, τ = RC.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Alternating current (AC) cannot be measured by DC ammeter because:
explanation: A DC ammeter measures average current. The average value of a symmetrical AC over a complete cycle is zero because it alternates between positive and negative values. Hence, a DC ammeter will show zero reading.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following gates is known as a universal gate?
explanation: NAND and NOR gates are called universal gates because any basic logic gate (AND, OR, NOT) and any complex logic circuit can be implemented using only NAND gates (or only NOR gates).

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Magnetic flux is a:
explanation: Magnetic flux (Φ = B·A = BA cos θ) is defined as the dot product of the magnetic field vector (B) and the area vector (A). The result of a dot product is a scalar quantity.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current:
explanation: In a pure inductor, the voltage across the inductor leads the current by 90° (or the current lags the voltage by 90°). This is because the induced EMF opposes the change in current.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following statements about a PN junction diode is correct?
option1: It allows current in both directions
option2: It allows current in one direction only
option3: It converts AC to DC automatically
explanation: A PN junction diode is a semiconductor device that allows current to flow easily in one direction (forward bias) and blocks current in the opposite direction (reverse bias). It acts as a rectifier.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The conductivity of a semiconductor:
option1: Increases with an increase in temperature
option2: Decreases with an increase in temperature
option4: Is same as that of a conductor
explanation: Semiconductors have a negative temperature coefficient of resistance. As temperature increases, more covalent bonds break, generating more free electrons and holes. This increases the number of charge carriers, thereby increasing conductivity.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The unit of reactance is the same as that of:
explanation: Reactance (inductive XL or capacitive XC) is the opposition to current in an AC circuit due to inductance or capacitance. It is measured in ohms (Ω), which is the same unit as resistance.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A wire of resistance R is stretched to double its length. Its new resistance will be:
explanation: Resistance R = ρL/A. When length is doubled (L' = 2L), volume remains constant, so A' = A/2. New resistance R' = ρ(2L) / (A/2) = ρL/A × 4 = 4R.

subject: physics

description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A galvanometer can be converted into a voltmeter by connecting a:
explanation: To convert a galvanometer into a voltmeter, a high resistance is connected in series with it. This limits the current through the galvanometer and allows the combination to measure large potential differences.

subject: physics

question: A galvanometer of resistance 50 Ω gives a full-scale deflection for a current of 5 mA. To convert it into a voltmeter of range 0-5 V, the required series resistance is:
explanation: For a voltmeter, V = Ig(G + R). So, 5 = (5 × 10⁻³)(50 + R). This gives 1000 = 50 + R, so R = 1000 - 50 = 950 Ω.

subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A point charge Q is placed at the center of a spherical Gaussian surface. The electric flux through the surface will change if:
option1: The sphere is replaced by a cube
option2: The point charge is moved off-center
option3: A second point charge is placed outside the sphere
option4: The point charge is replaced by a charge 2Q
explanation: According to Gauss's law, the net flux through a closed surface is proportional to the charge enclosed (Φ = Q/ε₀). Changing the shape (cube instead of sphere) or moving the charge inside doesn't change the total enclosed charge. Placing a charge outside doesn't change enclosed charge. Only changing Q to 2Q changes the enclosed charge and thus the flux.

subject: physics

question: In a step-up transformer, the current in the secondary coil is:
explanation: For an ideal transformer, power input = power output, so VpIp = VsIs. In a step-up transformer, Vs > Vp. Therefore, to maintain equal power, Is must be less than Ip.

explanation: Ohm's law: V = IR, so R = V/I = 2 V / 1 A = 2 Ω.

question: Two bulbs, one of 60 W and one of 100 W, are connected in series to a power supply. Which bulb will glow brighter?
explanation: When connected in series, the current is the same through both bulbs. Power dissipated P = I²R. The 60 W bulb has a higher resistance (since R = V²/P for same voltage rating). With same I, the higher resistance bulb (60 W) dissipates more power and glows brighter.

subject: physics

description: 2 advanced electricity & magnetism MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following has the highest penetrating power?
explanation: Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation. They have no charge and very high energy, allowing them to penetrate most materials deeply. Alpha particles have the lowest penetrating power.

question: The work done by a conservative force depends on:
option2: The initial and final positions only
explanation: Conservative forces (like gravity, spring force) do work that depends only on initial and final positions, not on the path taken between them.

question: According to de Broglie hypothesis, the wavelength associated with a particle of momentum p is:

explanation: Escape velocity v_e = √(2GM/R) ≈ 11.2 km/s for Earth.

question: The magnetic force on a charged particle moving parallel to a magnetic field is:
explanation: Magnetic force F = q(v × B) = qvB sinθ. When velocity is parallel to field, θ = 0°, sin0° = 0, so force = 0.

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If the momentum of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
explanation: KE = p²/2m. If p becomes 2p, KE becomes (2p)²/2m = 4p²/2m = 4 times original KE.

subject: physics

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A body moving with uniform acceleration covers 40 m in the first 4 seconds and 60 m in the next 4 seconds. Its initial velocity is:
explanation: Using s = ut + ½at²: For first 4s: 40 = 4u + 8a. For total 8s: 100 = 8u + 32a. Solving: u = 5 m/s, a = 2.5 m/s².

explanation: K_max = hν - φ, depends only on frequency ν (not intensity). Intensity affects photocurrent magnitude only.

question: The force between two parallel current-carrying conductors is:
option3: Attractive if currents are in same direction
option4: Repulsive if currents are in same direction
explanation: Parallel currents attract; antiparallel currents repel (Ampere's force law).

question: The gravitational potential energy of a satellite in circular orbit is:
explanation: Gravitational potential energy U = -GMm/r is always negative for bound orbits.

explanation: Torque τ = pE sinθ. Maximum when sinθ = 1 ⇒ θ = 90°.

explanation: Orbital velocity v₀ = √(GM/R) ≈ 7.9 km/s for low Earth orbit.

explanation: For elastic collision: v₁ = [(m₁-m₂)/(m₁+m₂)]u₁ = [(2-3)/(2+3)]×4 = (-1/5)×4 = -0.8 m/s.

explanation: de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p ∝ 1/p (inversely proportional to momentum).

explanation: Bohr's quantization: L = mvr = nħ = n(h/2π).

explanation: F/l = μ₀I₁I₂/2πr (attractive if currents parallel).

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The phenomenon of production of emf in a conductor moving in magnetic field is called:
explanation: Electromagnetic induction: emf induced due to relative motion between conductor and magnetic field.

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The rms velocity of oxygen molecules at temperature T is v. The rms velocity of hydrogen molecules at same temperature is:
explanation: v_rms ∝ 1/√M. M_O₂/M_H₂ = 32/2 = 16. So v_H₂/v_O₂ = √16 = 4. Therefore v_H₂ = 4v.

question: The critical velocity for turbulent flow in a pipe depends on:
explanation: Critical velocity v_c = (R_e η)/(ρD), depends on Reynolds number R_e, viscosity η, density ρ, and diameter D.

question: A body moving with uniform velocity has:
explanation: Uniform velocity means constant speed in a straight line. Since velocity is not changing, acceleration (rate of change of velocity) is zero.

question: The work done by a force acting perpendicular to the displacement is:
explanation: Work done W = F·d·cosθ, where θ is the angle between force and displacement vectors. When θ = 90°, cos90° = 0, so W = 0.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of Earth is approximately:
explanation: The standard value of acceleration due to gravity at Earth's surface is 9.8 m/s² (often approximated as 10 m/s² in calculations).

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Newton's first law of motion is also called:
explanation: Newton's first law states that a body at rest stays at rest and a body in motion continues in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force. This property of matter to resist changes in motion is called inertia.

subject: physics

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The kinetic energy of a body of mass 2 kg moving with velocity 3 m/s is:
explanation: Kinetic energy KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × (3)² = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 J.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The time period of a simple pendulum depends on:
explanation: Time period T = 2π√(l/g), where l is the length of pendulum and g is acceleration due to gravity. It is independent of mass and amplitude (for small angles).

explanation: de Broglie hypothesis: λ = h/p, where h is Planck's constant and p is momentum of the particle. This establishes wave-particle duality.

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A projectile launched at an angle θ with horizontal has maximum range when θ equals:
explanation: Range R = (v₀²sin2θ)/g. Maximum range occurs when sin2θ = 1, i.e., 2θ = 90°, so θ = 45°.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The centripetal force acting on a body moving in a circle of radius r with speed v is:
explanation: Centripetal force F = mv²/r, directed toward the center of the circle. It is required to keep the body in circular motion.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The principle of conservation of linear momentum is applicable when:
explanation: Conservation of linear momentum holds for an isolated system where net external force is zero. Internal forces do not affect the total momentum of the system.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The torque acting on an electric dipole placed in a uniform electric field is maximum when the angle between dipole moment and field is:
explanation: Torque τ = pE sinθ, where p is dipole moment, E is electric field, and θ is angle between them. τ is maximum when sinθ = 1, i.e., θ = 90°.

subject: physics

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A body of mass 5 kg is moving with velocity 4 m/s. Its momentum is:
explanation: Momentum p = mv = 5 × 4 = 20 kg·m/s.

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The force between two parallel current-carrying conductors is attractive when currents are:
explanation: Parallel conductors with currents in the same direction attract each other; with currents in opposite directions, they repel (Ampere's law).

subject: physics

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The velocity of sound is maximum in:
explanation: Velocity of sound v = √(Y/ρ) for solids, where Y is Young's modulus and ρ is density. Solids have much higher elastic modulus compared to liquids and gases, so sound travels fastest in solids (steel: ~5000 m/s) compared to water (~1500 m/s) and air (~340 m/s). Sound cannot travel in vacuum.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The Doppler effect for sound depends on:
option4: Relative motion of source and observer
explanation: Doppler effect for sound depends on velocities of source, observer, and medium relative to each other. Unlike light, sound requires a medium, so motion relative to medium matters.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The angular momentum of a rotating body is conserved when:
explanation: Conservation of angular momentum: If net external torque acting on a system is zero, total angular momentum remains constant.

subject: physics

question: The phase difference between displacement and acceleration in simple harmonic motion is:
explanation: In SHM: x = A sin(ωt), v = Aω cos(ωt), a = -Aω² sin(ωt) = Aω² sin(ωt+π). So acceleration leads displacement by π radians (180°).

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The maximum horizontal range of a projectile with initial velocity v is:
explanation: Maximum range Rₘₐₓ = v²/g (when θ = 45°).

question: The force acting on a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field is:
explanation: Magnetic force F = q(v × B). When v ⊥ B, force magnitude is qvB and direction is perpendicular to both v and B (given by right-hand rule).

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The period of oscillation of a mass m suspended from a spring of force constant k is:
explanation: For spring-mass system: T = 2π√(m/k).

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The energy stored in an inductor of inductance L carrying current I is:
explanation: Energy stored U = ½LI², analogous to ½CV² for capacitor and ½mv² for kinetic energy.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The apparent weight of a person in a lift accelerating upward is:
explanation: When lift accelerates upward with acceleration a, apparent weight = m(g+a) > mg (actual weight).

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The velocity of electromagnetic waves in vacuum is:
explanation: Speed of light (and all EM waves) in vacuum c = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The work done in moving a charge q through a potential difference V is:
explanation: Work done W = qV. This is the definition of electric potential difference: V = W/q.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends on:
explanation: KEmax = hf - φ, where φ is work function. It depends on frequency f, not intensity.

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The center of mass of a uniform triangular lamina lies at:
explanation: For uniform density objects, center of mass coincides with geometric center. For triangle, it's the centroid (intersection of medians), located at 2/3 the distance from each vertex to opposite side.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The ratio of escape velocity to orbital velocity for a satellite close to Earth's surface is:
explanation: Escape velocity vₑ = √(2GM/R), orbital velocity vₒ = √(GM/R). Therefore, vₑ/vₒ = √2.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The acceleration of a body moving with constant speed in a circle is:
option4: Constant in both magnitude and direction
explanation: Centripetal acceleration a = v²/r has constant magnitude but continuously changing direction (always toward center), so it's not constant.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The force between two point charges is governed by:
explanation: Coulomb's law: F = kq₁q₂/r², describing electrostatic force between stationary point charges.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The angular velocity of Earth about its axis is approximately:
explanation: Earth completes 2π radians in 24 hours = 86400 s. ω = 2π/86400 ≈ 6.28/86400 ≈ 7.27 × 10⁻⁵ rad/s.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The potential energy of a spring stretched by distance x is:
explanation: Elastic potential energy U = ½kx², where k is spring constant.

title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The maximum height attained by a projectile launched with velocity v at angle θ is:
explanation: Hₘₐₓ = (v sinθ)²/2g = v²sin²θ/2g.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The force experienced by a charged particle moving parallel to a magnetic field is:
explanation: F = q(v × B) = qvB sinθ. When θ = 0° (parallel), sin0° = 0, so F = 0.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The critical velocity for an object to orbit close to Earth's surface is approximately:
explanation: Orbital velocity near Earth's surface vₒ = √(gR) = √(9.8 × 6.4 × 10⁶) ≈ 7.9 km/s. Escape velocity = 11.2 km/s.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The angle between angular velocity and linear velocity in circular motion is:
explanation: Linear velocity v = ω × r is tangential (perpendicular to radius), while angular velocity ω is axial (perpendicular to plane of rotation). So angle between ω and v is 90°.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The work done by gravitational force when a satellite moves in circular orbit is:
explanation: Gravitational force acts radially inward while displacement is tangential (perpendicular). Since F ⊥ ds, work done dW = F·ds = 0.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The principle used in hydraulic brake system is:
explanation: Pascal's law: Pressure applied to confined fluid is transmitted undiminished to every portion of fluid and container walls. Hydraulic brakes use this principle to multiply force.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The rest mass of photon is:
explanation: Photons are massless particles that always travel at speed of light c in vacuum. Their rest mass is zero.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The torque on a dipole in uniform electric field is zero when angle between dipole moment and field is:
explanation: Torque τ = pE sinθ. τ = 0 when sinθ = 0, i.e., θ = 0° or 180°. At θ = 0°, dipole is in stable equilibrium.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The velocity of sound in air at 0°C is 331 m/s. Its velocity at 20°C is approximately:
explanation: v ∝ √T (absolute temperature). v₂/v₁ = √(T₂/T₁). T₁ = 273 K, T₂ = 293 K. v₂ = 331 × √(293/273) ≈ 331 × 1.036 ≈ 343 m/s.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations

question: The work done by a force is zero when the angle between force and displacement is:

explanation: Orbital velocity v₀ = √(GM/R) ≈ 7.9 km/s for low Earth orbit. Escape velocity is 11.2 km/s.

subject: physics

question: Body of mass 3 kg moving with velocity 6 m/s collides elastically with body of mass 2 kg at rest. After collision, velocity of first body is:
explanation: For elastic collision: v₁ = [(m₁-m₂)/(m₁+m₂)]u₁ = [(3-2)/(3+2)]×6 = (1/5)×6 = 1.2 m/s.

subject: physics

description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A projectile is fired at angle θ with horizontal. Its horizontal range is maximum when θ equals:
explanation: Range R = u²sin2θ/g. Maximum when sin2θ = 1 ⇒ 2θ = 90° ⇒ θ = 45°.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The slope of velocity-time graph gives:
explanation: Slope of v-t graph = dv/dt = acceleration. Area under v-t graph gives displacement.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Newton's first law of motion defines:
explanation: First law (law of inertia) states that a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by external force.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: When a body moves in a circular path with constant speed, its acceleration is:
option3: Constant in magnitude but changing direction
option4: Changing in both magnitude and direction
explanation: Centripetal acceleration a = v²/r has constant magnitude but direction always toward center, so continuously changing direction.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The work done by centripetal force on a body moving in circular path is:
explanation: Centripetal force is always perpendicular to displacement (tangential direction), so work done = F·d·cos90° = 0.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A body of mass m moving with velocity v has kinetic energy K. If mass is doubled and velocity halved, new kinetic energy is:
explanation: Original K = ½mv². New K' = ½(2m)(v/2)² = ½(2m)(v²/4) = ¼mv² = K/2.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The gravitational force between two masses is F. If distance between them is doubled, force becomes:
explanation: F ∝ 1/r². If r becomes 2r, F becomes F/4.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The Compton effect demonstrates:
explanation: Compton scattering (X-ray photons colliding with electrons) shows photons behave as particles with momentum p = h/λ.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The velocity of electron in first Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom is approximately:

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The angular momentum of electron in first Bohr orbit is:
explanation: L = n(h/2π). For n=1, L = h/2π = ħ.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The mass defect in nuclear reaction is the difference between:
explanation: Mass defect Δm = (sum of masses of free nucleons) - (mass of nucleus) = (mass of reactants) - (mass of products) for reaction.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The neutrino was postulated by Pauli to explain conservation of:
explanation: Neutrino (ν) postulated to conserve energy, momentum, and angular momentum in beta decay spectrum.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The nuclear force is:
explanation: Nuclear force is short range (~1-3 fm), charge independent (same for p-p, n-n, p-n), spin dependent, and strongest fundamental force (at < 1 fm).

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Heisenberg uncertainty principle for position and momentum is:
explanation: Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2, where ħ = h/2π. Some texts use Δx Δp ≥ h/4π which is equivalent.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following is a derived quantity?
explanation: Derived quantities are those that are expressed in terms of base quantities. Velocity is derived from length and time (m/s), whereas length, time, and mass are base quantities in the SI system.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
explanation: Scalar quantities are described by magnitude only. Speed is the magnitude of velocity and has no direction. Force, velocity, and displacement are vector quantities.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The resultant of two forces of equal magnitude 'F' acting at an angle of 120° is:
explanation: The magnitude of the resultant R = √(F² + F² + 2F² cos θ). For θ=120°, cos 120° = -1/2. So, R = √(2F² + 2F²(-1/2)) = √(2F² - F²) = √(F²) = F.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: An object is in uniform motion if it covers:
option1: Equal distances in equal intervals of time
option2: Equal displacements in equal intervals of time
option3: Unequal distances in equal intervals of time
explanation: Uniform motion implies constant velocity, which means both constant speed and constant direction. This is best described as equal displacements in equal intervals of time, regardless of how small the time interval is.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A car accelerates from rest at a constant rate of 2 m/s². The distance covered in the first 4 seconds is:
explanation: Using the second equation of motion for constant acceleration: s = ut + (1/2)at². Here, u=0, a=2 m/s², t=4 s. So, s = 0 + (1/2)×2×(4)² = (1/2)×2×16 = 16 m.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The slope of a velocity-time graph represents:
explanation: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity. On a velocity-time graph, the slope (Δv/Δt) directly gives the acceleration of the object.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards. At the highest point of its motion, its velocity and acceleration are:
explanation: At the highest point, the ball momentarily comes to rest, so its velocity is zero. However, the acceleration due to gravity (g) acts constantly downwards throughout its motion, so at the highest point, a = g downwards.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Two bodies of masses 2 kg and 4 kg are dropped from the same height. The ratio of their accelerations is:
explanation: In the absence of air resistance, all objects fall with the same constant acceleration due to gravity (g), regardless of their mass. Therefore, the ratio of their accelerations is 1:1.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A force of 10 N acts on a body of mass 2 kg for 3 seconds. The change in momentum of the body is:
explanation: Impulse (J) = Force × time = Change in momentum (Δp). Therefore, Δp = F × t = 10 N × 3 s = 30 Ns.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Newton's first law of motion is also called the law of:
explanation: Newton's first law states that an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force. This property of objects to resist changes in their motion is called inertia.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The work done by the centripetal force on a body moving in a circle is always:
explanation: Centripetal force acts towards the center of the circle, which is perpendicular to the direction of the instantaneous displacement (tangential) of the body. Work done W = F·d = F d cos θ. Since θ = 90°, cos 90° = 0, so work done is zero.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The kinetic energy of a body is quadrupled. Its momentum will become:
explanation: Kinetic energy K = p²/2m. If K becomes 4K, then p²/2m = 4 × (p_initial²/2m). This implies p² = 4 p_initial², so p = 2 p_initial. Momentum becomes double.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A 1 kg mass has a potential energy of 1 J relative to the ground at a height of nearly:
explanation: Potential energy P.E. = mgh. Given P.E. = 1 J, m = 1 kg, and g ≈ 10 m/s². Then h = P.E. / (mg) = 1 / (1×10) = 0.1 m.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Angular momentum is conserved when:
option1: No force acts on the body
option2: No torque acts on the body
explanation: Angular momentum (L) is conserved when the net external torque acting on the system is zero (τ = dL/dt = 0). Force can act without producing torque if applied at the axis or radially.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: An object rotating with a constant angular speed has:
explanation: Even with constant angular speed, the direction of the linear velocity vector changes continuously. This change in direction requires a centripetal acceleration (v²/r) directed towards the center. Tangential acceleration is zero only if angular speed is constant.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The moment of inertia of a body depends upon:
option2: Distribution of mass and axis of rotation
explanation: Moment of inertia (I) is the rotational analog of mass. It depends on the mass of the body and how that mass is distributed relative to the axis of rotation (I = Σ mr²).

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A body of mass 2 kg is moving with a velocity of 3 m/s. Its linear momentum is:
explanation: Linear momentum p = mass × velocity = 2 kg × 3 m/s = 6 kg m/s.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following is the correct relation between linear velocity (v) and angular velocity (ω)?
explanation: For a body moving in a circle of radius 'r', the linear velocity (v) is related to the angular velocity (ω) by the equation v = rω.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The value of 'g' at the center of the Earth is:
explanation: The acceleration due to gravity (g) inside the Earth is given by g' = g (1 - d/R), where d is the depth. At the center, d = R, so g' = g (1 - 1) = 0.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The orbital speed of a satellite very close to the Earth's surface is approximately:
explanation: The orbital velocity for a satellite close to Earth is given by v = √(GM/R). For Earth, this value is approximately 7.9 km/s, which is rounded to 8 km/s. The escape velocity is 11 km/s.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: An elevator is accelerating upwards. The apparent weight of a person inside it:
explanation: When the elevator accelerates upwards, the normal reaction from the floor (which is the apparent weight) increases. This is because the floor must push up with extra force to accelerate the person upwards. Apparent weight = m(g + a).

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The maximum velocity of a body in simple harmonic motion (SHM) is given by:
explanation: In SHM, velocity v = ω√(A² - x²). The velocity is maximum when the displacement x = 0 (at the mean position). So, v_max = ω√(A² - 0) = ωA.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The acceleration of a body in simple harmonic motion is directly proportional to:
explanation: In SHM, acceleration is directly proportional to the negative of displacement. a = -ω²x. The magnitude of acceleration is proportional to the displacement from the mean position.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The velocity of all electromagnetic waves in vacuum is:
explanation: In vacuum, all electromagnetic waves (radio, light, X-rays, etc.) travel at the same constant speed, denoted by 'c', which is approximately 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The resistance of a wire depends upon all of the following EXCEPT:
explanation: Resistance R = ρL/A. It depends on the material's resistivity (ρ), length (L), and cross-sectional area (A). Temperature affects resistivity. Resistance does not directly depend on the mass of the wire.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The force on a charge moving in a magnetic field is maximum when the angle between velocity and magnetic field is:
explanation: The magnetic force is given by F = qvB sin θ. The value of sin θ is maximum (1) when θ = 90°. So, the force is maximum when the charge moves perpendicular to the magnetic field.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by:
explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule (for motors) gives the direction of force acting on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field. The thumb, forefinger, and middle finger are mutually perpendicular, representing Force, Field, and Current.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Lenz's law is a consequence of the law of conservation of:
explanation: Lenz's law states that the induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it. This opposition means that work must be done against this opposing force, and this work is converted into electrical energy, thus conserving energy.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If the speed of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
explanation: Kinetic energy K = (1/2)mv². K is proportional to v². If v becomes 2v, then K becomes (2)² = 4 times the original kinetic energy.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: According to the kinetic molecular theory, the absolute temperature of a gas is proportional to the:
explanation: The average translational kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to the absolute temperature. KE_avg = (3/2)kT, where k is Boltzmann's constant.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The first law of thermodynamics is a statement of the conservation of:
explanation: The first law of thermodynamics (ΔU = Q - W) is essentially the law of conservation of energy applied to thermodynamic systems. It states that the change in internal energy of a system equals the heat added to the system minus the work done by the system.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The drift velocity of electrons in a conductor is of the order of:
explanation: Drift velocity is the average velocity attained by charged particles in a material due to an electric field. It is very slow, typically on the order of millimeters per second (10⁻⁴ to 10⁻³ m/s).

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A charge of 5 C moves with a velocity of 2 m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.1 T. The force experienced by it is:
explanation: The magnetic force is F = qvB sin θ. For perpendicular motion, θ = 90°, so sin 90° = 1. Therefore, F = 5 C × 2 m/s × 0.1 T × 1 = 1 N.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A body of mass 5 kg is acted upon by a constant force of 20 N. The acceleration produced is:
explanation: According to Newton's second law, F = ma. Therefore, a = F/m = 20 N / 5 kg = 4 m/s².

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is:
explanation: The range of a projectile is given by R = (u² sin 2θ)/g. The value of sin 2θ is maximum (1) when 2θ = 90°, so θ = 45°. At this angle, the range is maximum.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A stone is thrown horizontally from the top of a tower. The path of the stone is:
explanation: A body thrown horizontally from a height has an initial horizontal velocity but its vertical motion is under the influence of gravity (constant acceleration). This combination of uniform horizontal motion and accelerated vertical motion results in a parabolic trajectory.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is about:
explanation: Escape velocity (v_esc) is the minimum speed needed for an object to escape from a planet's gravitational influence without further propulsion. For Earth, v_esc = √(2GM/R) ≈ 11.2 km/s.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A 2 kg body and a 4 kg body have the same kinetic energy. The ratio of their linear momenta (p2kg : p4kg) is:
explanation: Since K = p²/2m, we have p = √(2mK). If K is constant, p ∝ √m. Therefore, p1/p2 = √(m1/m2) = √(2/4) = √(1/2) = 1/√2. So the ratio is 1 : √2.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 3: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If the distance between two point charges is halved, the force between them becomes:
explanation: According to Coulomb's law, F ∝ 1/r². If r becomes r/2, then r² becomes (r/2)² = r²/4. Therefore, the new force F' ∝ 1/(r²/4) = 4 × (1/r²). So, the force becomes four times.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A person standing on a frictionless horizontal surface throws a ball. The person will:
option2: Move in the direction of the throw
option3: Move opposite to the direction of the throw
explanation: This is based on Newton's third law and conservation of momentum. When the person exerts a force on the ball to throw it forward, the ball exerts an equal and opposite force on the person, pushing them backward.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A girl is sitting on a swing. Another girl sits by her side. The time period of the swing:
explanation: The time period of a simple pendulum (or swing) T = 2π√(L/g) depends only on its length (L) and the acceleration due to gravity (g). It is independent of the mass of the bob. Adding more mass does not change the time period.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If a motorcyclist doubles his speed on a circular turn of the same radius, the centripetal force required becomes:
explanation: Centripetal force F_c = mv²/r. For a constant mass (m) and radius (r), F_c ∝ v². If the speed (v) is doubled, the force becomes (2)² = 4 times the original force.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The value of Boltzmann's constant (k) is:
explanation: Boltzmann's constant (k) relates the average kinetic energy of particles in a gas with the temperature. Its value is 1.38 × 10⁻²³ joules per kelvin (J/K).

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: During a phase change (e.g., ice melting at 0°C), the temperature of the substance:
explanation: During a phase transition, the heat supplied (latent heat) is used to overcome the intermolecular forces to change the phase of the substance, not to increase the average kinetic energy of the molecules. Therefore, the temperature remains constant.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following properties of a wave is independent of the others?
explanation: Amplitude is a measure of the energy carried by the wave and is independent of the wave's frequency, wavelength, or velocity. The other three are related by the equation v = fλ.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The S.I. unit of momentum is:
explanation: Momentum (p = mv) has units of kg m/s. A Newton-second (N·s) is equivalent to (kg m/s²) × s = kg m/s, so it is the same unit.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In the equation F = ma, 'm' represents:
explanation: In Newton's second law of motion, F = ma, 'm' stands for the inertial mass of the object, which is a measure of its resistance to acceleration.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The value of 'g' is minimum at:
explanation: The value of 'g' is minimum at the equator. This is due to two reasons: the Earth's radius is larger at the equator (centrifugal force from rotation also reduces effective g), and the centrifugal force due to Earth's rotation is maximum at the equator.

question: X-rays are produced when:
option4: Alpha particles strike a metal target
explanation: X-rays are produced in an X-ray tube when high-speed electrons are accelerated and suddenly stopped by striking a metal target (usually tungsten or copper). The kinetic energy of the electrons is converted into X-ray radiation.
