description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A 5 kg mass is moving with a constant velocity of 2 m/s. The net force acting on it is:
explanation: According to Newton's first law, if a body is moving with constant velocity (no acceleration), the net external force acting on it must be zero.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The property of a body due to which it opposes any change in its state of rest or uniform motion is called:
explanation: Inertia is the natural tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion. This property is quantified by its mass.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following is an example of a non-conservative force?
explanation: A force is non-conservative if the work done by it depends on the path taken. Friction is a classic example, as longer paths result in more negative work done. Work done by conservative forces (gravity, spring) is path-independent.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A 0.5 kg ball is thrown upwards with a speed of 20 m/s. Its kinetic energy at the highest point is:
explanation: At the highest point, the vertical velocity of the ball becomes zero. Kinetic energy (KE = 1/2 mv²) is proportional to the square of velocity. Since v=0, the KE at that instant is zero.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A body moving with a constant speed in a circle:
explanation: Even with constant speed, the direction of velocity changes continuously. This change in direction constitutes an acceleration directed towards the center of the circle, called centripetal acceleration.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The mass of a body:
explanation: Mass is a fundamental property of matter and is a measure of its inertia. It is a scalar quantity that remains constant everywhere, regardless of location. Weight varies due to changes in 'g'.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The de Broglie wavelength associated with a moving particle is inversely proportional to its:
explanation: The de Broglie hypothesis states that every moving particle has a wave-like nature. Its wavelength λ is given by λ = h/p, where h is Planck's constant and p is the momentum of the particle. Therefore, λ ∝ 1/p.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A force of 10 N acts on a body for 5 seconds. The impulse is:
explanation: Impulse = Force × time = 10 N × 5 s = 50 Ns.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The rest mass of a photon is:
explanation: A photon is a massless particle. It always travels at the speed of light in vacuum and has zero rest mass. Its energy and momentum are carried by its frequency, not its mass.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If the distance between two bodies is increased by a factor of 4, the gravitational force between them becomes:
explanation: According to Newton's law of gravitation, F ∝ 1/r². If r becomes 4r, then r² becomes 16r². Therefore, the new force F' ∝ 1/(16r²) = (1/16) × (1/r²). So, the force becomes one-sixteenth of the original.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A body of mass m is moving in a circle of radius r with constant speed v. The work done by the centripetal force in half a revolution is:
explanation: The centripetal force is always perpendicular to the instantaneous displacement of the body. Work done W = F·d = F d cos 90° = 0. This is true for any displacement along the circular path.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The horizontal range of a projectile is the same for which two angles of projection?
explanation: The range R = (u² sin 2θ)/g. Since sin(2θ) = sin(180° - 2θ), the range is the same for complementary angles (θ and 90° - θ). 30° and 60° are complementary (30+60=90).

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The escape velocity from the surface of a planet does not depend upon:
explanation: Escape velocity v_esc = √(2GM/R). It depends on the mass (M) and radius (R) of the planet, and the gravitational constant (G). It is independent of the mass of the body trying to escape.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 20 m/s. The maximum height reached is (g=10 m/s²):
explanation: At maximum height, final velocity v=0. Using v² = u² - 2gh, we get 0 = (20)² - 2×10×h => 400 = 20h => h = 20 m.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If the speed of a car is halved, the stopping distance under the same braking force becomes:
explanation: Stopping distance is proportional to the square of the initial speed (from v² = 2as). If speed is halved (v/2), the distance becomes (1/2)² = 1/4 times the original distance.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following is the correct expression for the orbital velocity of a satellite near the Earth's surface?
explanation: Orbital velocity v₀ = √(GM/R). Since g = GM/R², we have GM = gR². Substituting, v₀ = √(gR²/R) = √(gR). Escape velocity is √(2gR).

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A particle is executing SHM with amplitude A. At what displacement from the mean position is its energy half kinetic and half potential?
explanation: Total energy E = (1/2)kA². Potential energy U = (1/2)kx². For U = E/2, we have (1/2)kx² = (1/2) × (1/2)kA² => x² = A²/2 => x = A/√2.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A 10 kg mass is lifted to a height of 5 m. The work done against gravity is (g=10 m/s²):
explanation: Work done against gravity = mgh = 10 kg × 10 m/s² × 5 m = 500 J.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If the momentum of a body is increased by 50%, its kinetic energy will increase by:
explanation: Let initial p = p. New p' = 1.5p. Initial K = p²/2m. New K' = (1.5p)²/2m = 2.25p²/2m = 2.25K. % increase = (2.25-1)×100 = 125%.

subject: physics
title: Mechanics & Motion — Part 4: 32 MCQs with Explanations
description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A bullet is fired from a gun. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the bullet to that of the gun (recoil) is:
option1: Equal to the ratio of their masses
option2: Equal to the ratio of their velocities
option3: Inversely proportional to the ratio of their masses
explanation: By conservation of momentum, m_b v_b = m_g v_g => v_g = (m_b/m_g)v_b. KE_b / KE_g = (1/2 m_b v_b²) / (1/2 m_g v_g²) = (m_b/m_g) × (v_b/v_g)² = (m_b/m_g) × (m_g/m_b)² = m_g/m_b. So, KE_b : KE_g = m_g : m_b.

description: 32 basic mechanics & motion MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A body of mass m is moving in a vertical circle of radius r with critical speed. The tension in the string at the highest point is:
explanation: At the highest point for critical speed (minimum speed to complete the circle), the centripetal force is provided entirely by the weight of the body. The tension (T) in the string becomes zero. mv²/r = mg.

question: A force is conservative if the work done by it:
option2: Is zero for a closed loop

explanation: A conservative force has the property that the work done by it around any closed path is zero. Equivalently, the work done is independent of the path and depends only on the initial and final positions.

explanation: A plane mirror always forms an image that is virtual (cannot be projected on a screen), erect (upright), and laterally inverted (left appears as right). The image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

option3: The image is formed behind the retina
explanation: Myopia (nearsightedness) occurs when the eyeball is too long or the eye lens is too curved. This causes the image of a distant object to be formed in front of the retina, making it appear blurry.

question: The electric field inside a uniformly charged spherical conductor is:
explanation: By Gauss's law and electrostatic shielding, electric field inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is zero everywhere.

explanation: Atomic number Z = number of protons = number of electrons in neutral atom.

explanation: Mass number A = number of protons (Z) + number of neutrons (N).

explanation: Longest wavelength (lowest energy) when electron falls from n=3 to n=2: 1/λ = R(1/2² - 1/3²) = 5R/36.

question: The binding energy of nucleus is the energy required to:
option2: Split nucleus into protons and neutrons
explanation: Binding energy = energy equivalent of mass defect = energy required to separate nucleus into its constituent protons and neutrons.

subject: physics

description: 40 intermediate physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The particle discovered by Chadwick in 1932 is:
explanation: Chadwick discovered neutron by bombarding beryllium with alpha particles: ⁹Be + ⁴He → ¹²C + ¹n.

description: 40 intermediate physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The penetrating power is maximum for:
explanation: Penetrating power: γ > β > α. Alpha stopped by paper; beta by few mm Al; gamma requires thick lead/concrete.

subject: physics

question: In beta decay, the atomic number of daughter nucleus:
explanation: In β⁻ decay: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄, so Z increases by 1, A unchanged. In β⁺ decay: p → n + e⁺ + ν, Z decreases by 1.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In alpha decay, the atomic number of daughter nucleus:
explanation: In α decay: parent → daughter + ⁴He, so Z decreases by 2, A decreases by 4.

subject: physics

description: 40 intermediate physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The liquid drop model of nucleus explains:
explanation: Liquid drop model (Bohr & Wheeler) treats nucleus as charged liquid drop; explains fission as deformation overcoming surface tension.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The shell model of nucleus explains:
explanation: Shell model (Mayer & Jensen) explains magic numbers (2,8,20,28,50,82,126) where nuclei exceptionally stable due to closed shells.

question: The energy required to remove electron from n=2 state of hydrogen atom is:
explanation: Ionization energy from n=2 = 0 - E₂ = 0 - (-3.4) = 3.4 eV.

explanation: Series limit (n=∞ → n=1): 1/λ = R(1 - 0) = R ⇒ λ = 1/R ≈ 91.2 nm.

explanation: E_n = -me⁴/(8ε₀²h²n²) ∝ -1/n².

question: The ionization energy of hydrogen-like atom with atomic number Z is proportional to:
explanation: E_n = -13.6 Z²/n² eV, so ionization energy from ground state = 13.6 Z² eV ∝ Z².

question: The number of significant figures in 0.00340 is:
explanation: Leading zeros (zeros to the left of the first non-zero digit) are not significant. The digits '3', '4', and the trailing zero after the decimal are significant, giving a total of 3 significant figures.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If the dot product of two vectors is zero, the vectors are:
explanation: The dot product A·B = |A||B|cos θ. For the product to be zero, cos θ must be 0, which means θ = 90°. Therefore, the vectors are perpendicular (orthogonal).

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 2: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 intermediate physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A vector of magnitude 10 units is added to a vector of magnitude 5 units. The magnitude of the resultant vector CANNOT be:
explanation: The magnitude of the resultant R must satisfy |A - B| ≤ R ≤ |A + B|. Here, the range is from |10-5|=5 to |10+5|=15. A value of 4 lies outside this range and is impossible.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The unit vector in the direction of a vector A is given by:
explanation: A unit vector has a magnitude of 1 and indicates direction. It is obtained by dividing a vector by its own magnitude: â = A / |A|.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: According to Kepler's law of periods, T² is proportional to:
explanation: Kepler's Third Law (Law of Periods) states that the square of the orbital period (T) of a planet is directly proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis (R) of its orbit. Mathematically, T² ∝ R³.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If the length of a simple pendulum is increased by four times, its time period becomes:
explanation: The time period of a simple pendulum is T = 2π√(L/g). T is proportional to √L. If L becomes 4L, then T becomes √4 = 2 times the original period.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: According to Einstein's mass-energy equivalence, 1 amu is equivalent to approximately:
explanation: Using Einstein's equation E = mc², the energy equivalent of 1 atomic mass unit (1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) is calculated to be about 931.5 mega-electronvolts (MeV).

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: An atom has 6 protons and 8 neutrons. Its mass number is:
explanation: Mass number (A) is the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus. A = Z + N = 6 + 8 = 14.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A semiconductor in its purest form is called:
explanation: An intrinsic semiconductor is a pure semiconductor material without any significant dopant atoms present. Examples include pure silicon or germanium.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The process of adding impurities to a pure semiconductor is called:
explanation: Doping is the intentional introduction of impurities into an intrinsic semiconductor to modulate its electrical properties. It creates either an excess of electrons (N-type) or holes (P-type).

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In a PN junction diode, the barrier potential is approximately 0.7 V for:
explanation: The built-in potential (barrier potential) across the depletion layer of a PN junction is about 0.7 V for silicon diodes and about 0.3 V for germanium diodes.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A logic gate that gives a HIGH output (1) only when all its inputs are HIGH (1) is:
explanation: The AND gate performs logical multiplication. Its output is true (1) only if all inputs are true (1). For example, for a 2-input AND gate, Y = A·B.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The truth table of which gate is the complement of the AND gate?
explanation: The NAND gate is the complement (NOT-AND) of the AND gate. Its output is the inverse of the AND gate output. It gives a LOW output only when all inputs are HIGH.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following has the highest modulus of elasticity?
explanation: Modulus of elasticity (Young's modulus) is a measure of the stiffness of a material. Steel has a very high Young's modulus (around 2 × 10¹¹ N/m²), meaning it requires a large stress to produce a small strain.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The entropy of a system:
option2: Always increases for a spontaneous process
explanation: According to the second law of thermodynamics, the total entropy of an isolated system can never decrease over time. It always increases for irreversible (spontaneous) processes and remains constant for reversible processes.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The number of electrons in the valence shell of a silicon atom is:
explanation: Silicon (Si) has an atomic number of 14. Its electronic configuration is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p². The outermost shell (n=3) contains 4 electrons (2 in the 3s and 2 in the 3p subshells).

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A 100 W electric bulb is used for 10 hours. The electrical energy consumed in kWh is:
explanation: Energy (in kWh) = Power (in kW) × Time (in hours). Power = 100 W = 0.1 kW. Time = 10 hours. Energy = 0.1 kW × 10 h = 1 kWh.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The vector product of two vectors is zero when they are:
explanation: The magnitude of the cross product is |A × B| = |A||B| sin θ. This is zero when sin θ = 0, which occurs when θ = 0° (parallel) or θ = 180° (anti-parallel).

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The binding energy per nucleon is maximum for nuclei with mass number around:
explanation: The binding energy per nucleon curve peaks at iron-56 (⁵⁶Fe). Nuclei around this mass number (A ≈ 50-60) are the most stable. Lighter and heavier nuclei have lower binding energy per nucleon.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In a double-slit experiment, the fringe spacing is:
option1: Directly proportional to the slit separation
option2: Inversely proportional to the slit separation
explanation: Fringe spacing (β) in Young's double-slit experiment is given by β = λD/d, where λ is wavelength, D is screen distance, and d is slit separation. Therefore, β is inversely proportional to d (slit separation).

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The basic building blocks of all matter are:
explanation: While atoms and molecules are the building blocks of matter we interact with, at a more fundamental level, protons and neutrons are made of quarks. According to the Standard Model, quarks and leptons are the fundamental particles.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The angle between two vectors A and B, if |A × B| = A·B, is:
explanation: Given |A × B| = |A||B| sin θ and A·B = |A||B| cos θ. For them to be equal, sin θ = cos θ. This occurs when tan θ = 1, i.e., when θ = 45° (or π/4 radians).

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The angular speed of the second's hand of a watch is:
explanation: The second's hand completes one revolution (2π radians) in 60 seconds. Therefore, angular speed ω = θ/t = 2π / 60 = π/30 rad/s.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom, the radius of the nth orbit is proportional to:
explanation: According to Bohr's postulates, the radius of the electron's orbit is given by r_n = n² a₀, where a₀ (0.529 Å) is the Bohr radius. Therefore, the radius is directly proportional to n².

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A stone is dropped from a height of 20 m. The time it takes to hit the ground is (g = 10 m/s²):
explanation: Using s = ut + (1/2)gt², where u=0, s=20 m, g=10 m/s². Then 20 = (1/2)×10×t² => 20 = 5t² => t² = 4 => t = 2 s.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The energy of the electron in the ground state of hydrogen atom is -13.6 eV. Its energy in the first excited state is:
explanation: In the Bohr model, energy Eₙ = -13.6/n² eV. The ground state is n=1. The first excited state is n=2. Therefore, E₂ = -13.6/2² = -13.6/4 = -3.4 eV.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The coefficient of linear expansion (α) and the coefficient of volume expansion (β) are related as:
explanation: For isotropic materials, the coefficient of volume expansion is approximately three times the coefficient of linear expansion: β = 3α.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: One kilowatt-hour (kWh) is a unit of:
explanation: 1 kWh is the energy consumed by a device of power 1 kW operating for 1 hour. It is a commercial unit of electrical energy. 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The time period of a seconds pendulum is:
explanation: A seconds pendulum is defined as a pendulum whose time period is exactly 2 seconds. It takes 1 second for a swing from one extreme to the other and 1 second to return.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The phenomenon in which a nucleus emits an electron is called:
explanation: Beta-minus (β⁻) decay involves the emission of an electron and an antineutrino from the nucleus, which results from the conversion of a neutron into a proton.

subject: physics
title: Physics — Mixed Practice — Part 3: 28 MCQs with Explanations
description: 28 basic physics — mixed practice MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The number of electrons in a neutral atom of atomic number 17 is:
explanation: In a neutral atom, the number of electrons is equal to the number of protons. The number of protons is given by the atomic number (Z). Therefore, if Z=17, there are 17 electrons.

question: In an adiabatic process for an ideal gas, which relation holds true?
explanation: For adiabatic process (no heat exchange), PV^γ = constant, where γ = Cp/Cv.

subject: physics

description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The ratio of specific heats (γ) for a diatomic gas at room temperature is:
explanation: For diatomic gas: C_v = 5R/2, C_p = 7R/2, so γ = C_p/C_v = 7/5 = 1.40.

subject: physics

description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In an isothermal process for an ideal gas, the internal energy:
explanation: For ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature. In isothermal process, ΔT = 0, so ΔU = 0.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If the temperature of a black body is doubled, the energy radiated per second increases by a factor of:
explanation: Stefan-Boltzmann law: P ∝ T⁴. If T doubles, P increases by 2⁴ = 16 times.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The efficiency of a heat engine cannot be 100% according to:
explanation: Second law (Kelvin-Planck statement) states that no heat engine can convert all heat into work in a cyclic process.

question: The root mean square speed of gas molecules is proportional to:
explanation: From kinetic theory: vᵣₘₛ = √(3RT/M), so vᵣₘₛ ∝ √T, where T is absolute temperature and M is molar mass.

question: The ratio of specific heats (γ = Cp/Cv) for a diatomic gas is:
explanation: For diatomic gases (at room temperature): degrees of freedom f = 5 (3 translational + 2 rotational). γ = 1 + 2/f = 1 + 2/5 = 7/5 = 1.4.

question: The heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of water by 1°C is:
explanation: Specific heat capacity of water = 1 cal/g°C = 1 kcal/kg°C = 4186 J/kg°C ≈ 4200 J/kg°C. So 1 kg water requires 1 kilocalorie (or 4200 J) to raise temperature by 1°C.

question: The efficiency of a Carnot engine cannot be 100% because:

explanation: Efficiency η = 1 - T₂/T₁. For η = 1, either T₂ = 0 K (impossible per third law of thermodynamics) or T₁ = ∞ (impossible). Also, Kelvin-Planck statement of second law forbids 100% conversion of heat to work in cyclic process.

question: The ratio of specific heat at constant pressure to specific heat at constant volume for monoatomic gas is:
explanation: For monoatomic gases: Cp = 5R/2, Cv = 3R/2, so γ = Cp/Cv = 5/3 ≈ 1.67.

explanation: For monatomic gas: C_v = 3R/2, C_p = 5R/2, so γ = C_p/C_v = 5/3 ≈ 1.67.

subject: physics

question: The process by which unstable nucleus emits radiation to become more stable is called:
explanation: Radioactivity (discovered by Becquerel, 1896) is spontaneous emission of α, β, or γ radiation by unstable nuclei.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The greenhouse effect is caused primarily by absorption of infrared radiation by:
explanation: CO₂ and H₂O vapor absorb infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface, trapping heat in atmosphere.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The ozone layer absorbs most of:
explanation: Ozone (O₃) in stratosphere absorbs harmful UV-B and UV-C radiation (200-310 nm), protecting life on Earth.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In an isothermal process for an ideal gas:
explanation: 'Isothermal' means 'at constant temperature'. In an isothermal process, the temperature of the system remains constant throughout. For an ideal gas, this implies that internal energy (ΔU = 0) does not change.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A heat engine converts:
explanation: A heat engine is a device that takes in heat from a hot reservoir, converts part of it into useful work (like moving a piston), and rejects the remaining waste heat to a cold reservoir.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The temperature at which the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales read the same value is:
explanation: To find where °C = °F, use the conversion formula: F = (9/5)C + 32. Substitute F = C: C = (9/5)C + 32. Solving gives C - (9/5)C = 32 => (-4/5)C = 32 => C = -40°. So, -40°C = -40°F.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In an adiabatic process, which of the following remains constant?
explanation: An adiabatic process is one in which no heat is exchanged between the system and its surroundings (Q = 0). This does not mean temperature is constant (that's isothermal). The total heat content is not a defined state function.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The efficiency of a Carnot engine depends only on:
option1: The nature of the working substance
option2: The temperatures of the source and sink
explanation: Carnot's theorem states that the efficiency of a Carnot engine (the most efficient heat engine) depends solely on the absolute temperatures of the hot reservoir (T₁) and the cold reservoir (T₂): η = 1 - T₂/T₁.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: At absolute zero temperature, a pure crystalline solid has:
explanation: The Third Law of Thermodynamics states that the entropy of a perfect crystal at absolute zero temperature is exactly zero. At 0 K, there is only one possible microstate (perfect order), so entropy S = k ln W = k ln 1 = 0.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The law that relates the pressure, volume, and temperature of an ideal gas is called:
explanation: The ideal gas law (PV = nRT) combines Boyle's law (P ∝ 1/V), Charles's law (V ∝ T), and Avogadro's law (V ∝ n) into a single equation of state for an ideal gas.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: If the absolute temperature of a black body is doubled, the total energy radiated per second per unit area becomes:
explanation: According to Stefan-Boltzmann law, the total energy radiated per second per unit area (E) is proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature: E = σT⁴. If T becomes 2T, then E becomes (2)⁴ = 16 times.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In a nuclear reactor, the function of the moderator is to:
explanation: The moderator (like graphite or heavy water) slows down the fast neutrons produced in fission to thermal neutrons. Thermal neutrons are more effective at causing further fission in U-235.

subject: physics
title: Heat & Thermodynamics: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate heat & thermodynamics MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The specific heat capacity of a substance is:
option2: The heat required to melt it
option3: Heat required to raise temperature of 1 kg by 1 K
option4: Heat required to raise temperature by 1°C regardless of mass
explanation: Specific heat capacity is defined as the amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of a unit mass (1 kg) of a substance by one degree kelvin (or one degree Celsius).

subject: physics
title: Units, Measurement & Vectors: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate units, measurement & vectors MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: What is the dimensional formula of angular momentum?
explanation: Angular momentum L = r × p, where r has dimension [L] and p (linear momentum) has dimension [M L T^-1]. Therefore, L = [L] × [M L T^-1] = [M L^2 T^-1].

subject: physics
title: Units, Measurement & Vectors: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate units, measurement & vectors MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The unit of coefficient of viscosity is:
explanation: Coefficient of viscosity η has SI unit Ns/m² or Pa·s (Pascal-second).

question: The SI unit of electric flux is:
explanation: Electric flux Φ = E·A has units N/C × m² = Nm²/C. Since 1 N/C = 1 V/m, units also = Vm.

subject: physics

explanation: Planck's constant h has dimensions [M L² T⁻¹], same as angular momentum.

explanation: Magnetic flux Φ has SI unit Weber (Wb). 1 Wb = 1 T·m².

question: The SI unit of electric current is:
explanation: The SI base unit of electric current is the ampere (A), defined as the constant current that would produce a force of 2×10⁻⁷ newtons per meter of length between two parallel conductors placed 1 meter apart in vacuum.

subject: physics
title: Units, Measurement & Vectors: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate units, measurement & vectors MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The dimensional formula of force is:
explanation: Force = mass × acceleration. Mass has dimension [M], acceleration has dimension [LT⁻²]. Therefore, force has dimensional formula [M][LT⁻²] = [MLT⁻²].

question: The unit of power in SI system is:
explanation: Power is the rate of doing work. SI unit of power is watt (W), where 1 W = 1 J/s.

explanation: Magnetic flux Φ = B·A (for uniform field perpendicular to area). SI unit is weber (Wb), where 1 Wb = 1 T·m².

question: The ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain is called:
explanation: Poisson's ratio σ = (lateral strain)/(longitudinal strain). It is dimensionless and typically between 0 and 0.5 for most materials.

question: The unit of gravitational field strength is:
explanation: Gravitational field strength g = F/m has units N/kg, which is dimensionally equivalent to m/s² (acceleration).

explanation: SI unit is becquerel (Bq = 1 decay/s). Traditional unit is curie (Ci = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq). Both are units of radioactivity (decay rate).

explanation: SI unit of inductance is henry (H). 1 H = 1 Wb/A = 1 V·s/A.

explanation: Magnetic flux Φ has SI unit Weber (Wb). 1 Wb = 1 T·m². Tesla is unit of magnetic field; Gauss is CGS unit of magnetic field.

explanation: Becquerel (Bq) = 1 disintegration per second. Curie (Ci) = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq (activity of 1g radium).

explanation: The prefix 'nano' represents 10⁻⁹. Therefore, 1 nanosecond = 10⁻⁹ seconds.

description: 29 intermediate units, measurement & vectors MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: One tesla (1 T) is equal to:
explanation: The tesla is the SI unit of magnetic flux density (B). It is defined as one weber per square meter (Wb/m²). It can also be expressed as 1 N/(A·m).

subject: physics
title: Units, Measurement & Vectors: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate units, measurement & vectors MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The SI unit of electric field intensity is:
explanation: Electric field intensity (E) is defined as force per unit charge (N/C). It is also defined as the potential gradient (V/m). Both N/C and V/m are equivalent SI units for the electric field.

subject: physics
title: Units, Measurement & Vectors: 29 MCQs with Explanations
description: 29 intermediate units, measurement & vectors MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: A wire of resistivity ρ is stretched to three times its original length. Its new resistivity will be:
explanation: Resistivity (ρ) is an intrinsic property of the material. It depends on the nature of the material and temperature, but not on the dimensions (length or cross-sectional area) of the wire. Therefore, it remains ρ.

question: The radioactive decay constant λ has units of:
explanation: The decay constant λ represents the probability per unit time that a nucleus will decay. From the decay law N = N₀e⁻λt, the exponent must be dimensionless. Therefore, λ must have units of 1/time, such as s⁻¹.

explanation: Planck's constant has units of energy × time (J·s). Energy has dimensions [ML²T⁻²]. Multiplying by time [T] gives [ML²T⁻¹].

explanation: When source approaches observer, waves get compressed, wavelength decreases, frequency increases.

description: 40 basic waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The phenomenon of light bending around obstacles is called:
explanation: Diffraction is the bending of waves around obstacles or through openings.

question: A particle executes SHM with time period T. The time taken to go from mean position to half the amplitude is:
explanation: In SHM, x = A sin(ωt). For x = A/2: A/2 = A sin(ωt) ⇒ sin(ωt) = 1/2 ⇒ ωt = π/6 ⇒ t = T/12.

explanation: Stopping potential V₀ = (h/e)ν - φ/e depends on frequency ν and work function φ, not on intensity.

explanation: Since v = c/n and frequency remains constant, λₘ = v/f = (c/n)/f = λ₀/n, where λ₀ is wavelength in vacuum.

explanation: Planck's quantum theory: E = hf, where h is Planck's constant (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s).

explanation: At resonance, inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance: ωL = 1/ωC, so ω = 1/√(LC).

description: 40 basic waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.

explanation: Photoelectric effect is emission of electrons (photoelectrons) from material upon electromagnetic radiation exposure above threshold frequency.

question: The frequency of AC mains supply in Pakistan is:
explanation: Standard frequency for AC power supply in Pakistan and most of Europe/Asia is 50 Hz. North America uses 60 Hz.

explanation: Q = ω₀L/R = 1/(ω₀CR) = resonant frequency/bandwidth. High Q means sharp resonance peak.

question: The form factor of sinusoidal AC is:
explanation: Form factor = V_rms/V_avg (for half-cycle). For sine wave: V_rms = V₀/√2, V_avg = 2V₀/π, so form factor = π/(2√2) ≈ 1.11.

subject: physics

question: The peak factor (crest factor) of sinusoidal AC is:
explanation: Peak factor = V₀/V_rms = √2 ≈ 1.414 for sine wave.

question: The electromagnetic waves used in radar are:
explanation: Microwaves (wavelength ~1 mm to 30 cm) are used in radar due to their ability to penetrate atmosphere and reflect from objects.

question: The waves that require a material medium for their propagation are called:
explanation: Mechanical waves require a medium to travel because they propagate through the vibration of material particles. Examples include sound waves, water waves, and waves on a string.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The speed of sound in air at 0°C is approximately:
explanation: The speed of sound in air at 0°C is 332 m/s. It increases with an increase in temperature. 340 m/s is the approximate speed at room temperature (around 20°C).

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: When two waves of the same frequency and amplitude meet in opposite phase, they produce:
explanation: Destructive interference occurs when the crest of one wave meets the trough of another wave (phase difference of 180° or π radians). If they have the same amplitude, they cancel each other out completely.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The phenomenon of beats is a result of:
option1: Superposition of two waves of slightly different frequencies
explanation: Beats are the periodic variation in amplitude at a point due to the superposition of two waves having slightly different frequencies. The beat frequency is the difference between the two frequencies.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 1: 40 MCQs with Explanations
description: 40 basic waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In stationary waves, the points where the amplitude is minimum are called:
explanation: Nodes are points in a standing wave that remain stationary (zero amplitude). They occur at points where destructive interference consistently happens. Antinodes are points of maximum amplitude.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The fundamental frequency of a vibrating string is 256 Hz. If the length is doubled, the new fundamental frequency will be:
explanation: For a string fixed at both ends, frequency f ∝ 1/L. If length L is doubled, the frequency becomes half. Therefore, new frequency = 256 Hz / 2 = 128 Hz.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: According to the Doppler effect, the apparent frequency of sound increases when the source and observer are:
explanation: When a source of sound and an observer move towards each other, the number of wavefronts received per second increases. This results in an increase in the observed frequency.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The energy of a photon is given by:
explanation: The energy (E) of a photon is directly proportional to its frequency (f): E = hf. Since frequency f = c/λ, where c is the speed of light and λ is the wavelength, we get E = hc/λ.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In a half-wave rectifier, the output frequency is:
explanation: In a half-wave rectifier, only one half of the input AC cycle is allowed to pass. The output waveform consists of pulses for each positive half-cycle. Therefore, the frequency of the output ripple is the same as the input AC frequency (e.g., 50 Hz).

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following is NOT a mode of heat transfer?
explanation: Heat is transferred via three main modes: conduction (through solids), convection (through fluids), and radiation (via electromagnetic waves). Absorption is a process by which a material takes in energy, not a mode of transfer.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The speed of sound is maximum in:
explanation: Sound travels fastest in solids because the particles are more tightly bound, allowing vibrations to transfer more quickly. It is slowest in gases. Speed in steel >> speed in water >> speed in air.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Nodes and antinodes are formed in:
explanation: A stationary wave (standing wave) is characterized by points of zero displacement called nodes and points of maximum displacement called antinodes, formed by the superposition of two identical waves traveling in opposite directions.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The photoelectric effect supports the:
explanation: The photoelectric effect could not be explained by the wave theory of light. Einstein explained it using the quantum theory, proposing that light consists of discrete packets of energy called photons.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In a series LCR circuit, at resonance, the impedance is:
explanation: At resonance, the inductive reactance (XL) equals the capacitive reactance (XC). They cancel each other out, so the impedance Z = √(R² + (XL - XC)²) becomes purely resistive and equal to R, which is the minimum possible impedance.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the highest frequency?
explanation: The electromagnetic spectrum is arranged by frequency and wavelength. Gamma rays have the highest frequency and shortest wavelength, followed by X-rays and then ultraviolet rays.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: When a ray of light enters from air into a glass slab, its wavelength:
explanation: When light enters a denser medium (glass) from a rarer medium (air), its speed (v) and wavelength (λ) decrease. However, its frequency (f) remains constant because it depends on the source. v = fλ, so if v decreases, λ must also decrease.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In a series resonant circuit, the power factor is:
explanation: At resonance, the circuit is purely resistive because the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel out. For a purely resistive circuit, the phase angle φ = 0°, so the power factor cos φ = 1.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: The phenomenon of polarization of light proves that light waves are:
explanation: Polarization is a property of transverse waves. Longitudinal waves (like sound) cannot be polarized because their vibration is parallel to the direction of propagation. Polarization confirms that light waves are transverse in nature.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: In a photoelectric experiment, the stopping potential depends on:
explanation: The stopping potential (V₀) is given by eV₀ = hf - φ, where f is the frequency and φ is the work function. While it depends on the work function, for a given metal, it varies linearly with the frequency of the incident light. It is independent of intensity.

subject: physics
title: Waves & Sound — Part 2: 16 MCQs with Explanations
description: 16 intermediate waves & sound MCQs with answers and explanations for MDCAT, FSc, PPSC preparation.
question: Two waves of the same frequency and amplitude traveling in opposite directions produce:
explanation: When two identical waves traveling in opposite directions superimpose, they produce a stationary wave (standing wave). The wave appears to be standing still with nodes and antinodes.

question: The frequency of A.C. mains in Pakistan is:
explanation: In Pakistan, as in many parts of the world (Europe, Asia), the standard frequency for alternating current (AC) mains electricity is 50 Hz.
